abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cultures of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) replicate in vivo conditions more accurately than two-dimensional (2D) cultures. This protocol outlines a simple and cost-efficient approach for generating mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) spheroids, which typically form within 1-3 days and are suitable for endothelial differentiation. Accutase can be applied to dissociate the spheroids into single cells for downstream analysis. A combination of growth factors is used to induce the differentiation of MSC spheroids into endothelial-like structures, which express key endothelial markers such as von Willebrand factor (vWF) and CD31, as confirmed by immunofluorescence.
